t: That, in accordance with section 5581 of the Revised Statutes of the United States 20 U.S.C. 43), the vacancy on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution, in the class other than Members of Congress, occurring by reason of the resignation of Ira Michael Heyman of California on May 27, 1994, is filled by the appointment of Louis Gerstner of Connecticut. The appointment is for a term of six years and shall take effect on the date on which this joint resolution becomes law.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is a bare personnel appointment with no consultation process, so it is not participation. But the seat is expressly in the citizen class "other than Members of Congress", so it places a private individual from outside the federal government on the board that governs a federal institution. That resembles a board with non-federal members taking part in federal decisions, unlike a board of salaried federal officials. The call is close because the section does not describe any specific decision the board will make.
fable.s: the vacancy on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution, in the class other than Members of Congress, occurring by reason of the resignation of Ira Michael Heyman of California on May 27, 1994, is filled by the appointment of Louis Gerstner of Connecticut

qwen_block.w: This section is a specific legislative appointment of an individual to a board. It does not establish a process for public participation, consultation, or advisory input from outside parties into a federal decision. The appointment itself is a unilateral action by Congress, and the text does not describe any mechanism for outsiders to participate in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: the vacancy on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution, in the class other than Members of Congress, occurring by reason of the resignation of Ira Michael Heyman of California on May 27, 1994, is filled by the appointment of Louis Gerstner of Connecticut.

opus.w: This section only fills a vacancy on the Smithsonian's governing Board of Regents by appointing a named person. It creates no process, such as a comment period, hearing, advisory input or consultation, through which outside parties feed into a federal decision. The seat is held by a private citizen, but serving on the institution's own governing board is like the agency board members in the NLRB example, not outside participation. The appointment itself is a decision by Congress, which is inside the federal government.
opus.s: the vacancy on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution, in the class other than Members of Congress, occurring by reason of the resignation of Ira Michael Heyman of California on May 27, 1994, is filled by the appointment of Louis Gerstner of Connecticut.
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading:** The Board of Regents seat being filled is in the class "other than Members of Congress," so the appointee is a private citizen. That could look like an outsider being brought into federal decisions.

2. **Why it fails:** The joint resolution only names someone to a vacant seat on the Smithsonian's own governing board. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing or advisory process before any federal decision. A regent who governs the institution is doing the job of its governing body, much like the board members in the NLRB example (Example 7). That is not outside participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the appointment of an individual to the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution. The Board of Regents is the governing body of a federal institution, and its members are considered federal officials or part of the federal government structure. The definition states that federal officials are inside the federal government. Therefore, appointing a member to this board does not constitute participation by an outside party in a federal decision. It is an internal personnel action.
qwen_chat.s: the vacancy on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution... is filled by the appointment of Louis Gerstner of Connecticut.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that appointing a private citizen (Louis Gerstner) to the Board of Regents constitutes "participation" because it involves an outside person serving on a federal body. However, the definition explicitly states that federal officials and employees are inside the government. Members of the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution are federal appointees who serve as part of the federal government's governance structure, not as external consultants or advisory committee members bringing outside perspective into a specific decision-making process in the manner defined (e.g., advisory boards with non-federal members influencing a specific decision, public hearings, etc.). More importantly, this text is merely an appointment resolution, not a procedural requirement for participation in a decision. The definition emphasizes "consult or coordinate... before making a decision." This text is the act of filling a vacancy, not a process of participation. Furthermore, the Board of Regents is the governing body of the Smithsonian, a federal institution. Its members are effectively federal officials. The definition says "Congress, its committees and members, federal agencies, federal officials, and federal employees are all INSIDE the federal government." Appointing a federal official is not participation.
